en.title: Mild day in Italy: the snow retreats to 2,000 m
en.description: Mild day in Italy: the snow retreats to 2,000 m. Snow cover, new snow, resorts and the days ahead in Italy on 17 November.
en.lede: Yesterday about 21,210 km² was white in Italy; today 12,540 km² is left, 8,670 km² less in one day.

sections.h: A mild day eats the snow
p: Mild air hits the thin snow of the valleys first. Expect wet, heavy snow low down in the afternoon and firm, icy patches the next morning.
In Italy, about 12,540 km² of high ground is white today, down 8,670 km² on yesterday. That is 13 % of the high ground we map in Italy.

sections.h: From the valleys to the summits
p: Average depth of the snowpack by height band: 1,500-2,000 m: on average under 1 cm (17 % of the ground white); 2,000-2,500 m: on average 5 cm (78 % of the ground white); above 2,500 m: on average 20 cm (99 % white).

sections.h: The resorts with the most snow
p: At the top of the list, La Thuile ski reports 50 cm.
Then come Prali (49 cm), Courmayeur (42 cm), Schnalstal (39 cm) and Passo Stelvio (37 cm).
At La Thuile ski: 65 cm of fresh snow over three days, 89 cm more expected by Friday 20 November.
At Prali: 18 cm of fresh snow over three days, 32 cm more expected by Friday 20 November.
122 of the 237 resorts we follow in Italy have snow on their upper slopes.

The rest of the shortlist: Courmayeur: 42 cm on top, 65 cm in three days, 100 cm expected; Schnalstal: 39 cm on top, 5 cm in three days, 9 cm expected; Passo Stelvio: 37 cm on top, 6 cm in three days, 8 cm expected.
The week ahead could bring up to 58 cm, 48 cm of it in the next three days.
The snowiest day looks like Thursday 19 November, with up to 24 cm in the snowiest spots.
The second week adds up to 41 cm where it snows most.
The new snow freshens the upper slopes; lower down it may already be heavy or wet.
With more snow in the forecast, the next days should improve things further.

sections.h: How much of the country is white
p: Below about 2,000 m the slopes are mostly green or brown. Seven days ago the figure was 21,840 km², 9,300 km² more than now.
In the last 72 hours the most new snow, up to 31 cm, fell over the Aosta Valley, the Piedmont Alps and the central Apennines.
The last 24 hours alone brought up to 18 cm.
About 6,690 km² received at least 5 cm.

Here is how the deepest resorts compare with their usual 17 November: La Thuile ski: 29 cm at about 2,038 m, against 24 cm in a normal year; Prali: 15 cm at about 2,173 m, against 12 cm in a normal year; Courmayeur: 40 cm at about 1,976 m, against 21 cm in a normal year; Schnalstal: 23 cm at about 2,602 m, against 45 cm in a normal year.
3 of these 4 resorts are above their usual depth for the date.
These depths are for one height on each mountain, below the top, so they read lower than the upper-slope numbers further down.
In past winters the best snow at La Thuile ski usually came late February / early March.

For comparison, the neighbours on the same day: Austria: 30 % white, deepest Kühtai with 54 cm, up to 47 cm in the week ahead; Switzerland: 41 % white, deepest Glacier 3000 with 46 cm, up to 85 cm in the week ahead.

sections.h: Planning a day on the snow
p: Above 2,500 m the ground is almost fully white (99 % covered), so runs up there have a continuous base.
Between 2,000 m and 2,500 m the cover is patchy, about 78 % white: expect grass and stones between the snow.
Below 1,500 m the slopes are still almost bare.
If you can choose the day, go after Thursday 19 November: the fresh snow then has time to settle and the roads to be cleared.

advice: Roads to the higher resorts may need winter tyres or chains.
Check the resort's own lift status before you travel.
Fresh snow on a cold base sticks badly: take care on steep slopes.

it.title: Situazione neve in Italia, 17 novembre 2026: località, neve fresca e prossimi giorni
it.description: Neve in Italia il 17 novembre: manto nevoso, neve fresca, altezza per quota, prossimi giorni e migliori località.
it.lede: In Italia oggi circa 12.540 km² sono innevati (martedì 17 novembre). Sono 8.670 km² in meno rispetto a ieri.

p: Il terreno è per lo più bianco da circa 2.000 m in su. Sette giorni fa la superficie era di 21.840 km², 9.300 km² in più di adesso.

sections.h: Dove è caduta la neve fresca
p: La neve fresca più abbondante nelle ultime 72 ore: fino a 31 cm. Zone: Valle d'Aosta, Alpi piemontesi e Appennino centrale.
Solo nelle ultime 24 ore sono caduti fino a 18 cm.
Almeno 5 cm di neve fresca coprono circa 6.690 km².
La neve fresca sul fondo regala curve morbide in quota; più in basso resta a chiazze.

Altezza media del manto nevoso per fascia di quota: 1.500–2.000 m: in media meno di 1 cm (17 % innevato); 2.000–2.500 m: in media 5 cm (78 % innevato); sopra i 2.500 m: in media 20 cm (99 % innevato).
In testa c'è La Thuile ski: 50 cm nella parte alta delle piste.
Seguono: Prali (49 cm), Courmayeur (42 cm), Schnalstal (39 cm) e Passo Stelvio (37 cm).
La Thuile ski: 65 cm di neve fresca in tre giorni e fino a 89 cm in più entro venerdì, 20 novembre.
Previsione di neve fresca: fino a 48 cm in tre giorni e fino a 58 cm in sette giorni.
Il giorno più nevoso: giovedì, 19 novembre, fino a 24 cm.
Più avanti, nei giorni 8–14, sui pendii più innevati possono aggiungersi fino a 41 cm.

advice: A inizio stagione la neve sulle rocce è sottile: restate sulle piste battute.
Sopra il limite del bosco la neve può essere ventata: attenzione sulle creste.
